question: How does methanol influence the hydrogen bonding between water and amide groups in poly(N-isopropylacrylamide)?
answer: Methanol disrupts hydrogen bond formation between water and the amide groups of poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM). This disruption reduces the energetic penalty associated with PNIPAM collapse in pure water, facilitating polymer collapse in water/methanol mixtures.  Methanol preferentially interacts with the isopropyl groups of PNIPAM through hydrophobic and van der Waals interactions, creating a methanol-rich local solvent environment around the polymer chain.
